newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE to start trade earlier on "tankan" days.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE to start trade earlier on "tankan" days.

text.p: The Tokyo International Financial Futures Exchange (TIFFE) is planning to allow trading in three-month Euroyen futures contracts to begin earlier than usual on days on which the Bank of Japan releases its quarterly "tankan" business survey, a TIFFE official said on Monday.

TIFFE will allow trade to begin at 8.45 a.m. (2345 GMT) rather than the usual 9 a.m. (0000 GMT) on such days, beginning with the next survey in early April, said Hiroshi Fujimoto, manager of TIFFE's Marketing and Research Section.
The BOJ releases its tankan at 8.50 a.m. (2350 GMT).
Trading hours on other days will remain unchanged for the time being, Fujimoto said.
TIFFE's regular trading hours are from 9 a.m. to 11.30 a.m. (0000 to 0230 GMT) in the morning and 12.30 p.m. to 3.30 p.m. (0330 to 0630 GMT) in the afternoon.
The proposal to start trade earlier than usual on tankan dates reflected the market's needs, Fujimoto said.

"Members (of TIFFE) say they want trade to start earlier on tankan dates because of the possibility that the market will be affected by it," he said. The plan is likely to be finalised at the next meeting of TIFFE's board of directors, he said.
